Baselines and records

What was on this land, and roughly when

Before financial close, an acquisition or a site decision, someone will ask what this land looked like before. We assemble the documented history of a parcel, route or site from archived satellite imagery and open datasets, showing what was built, cleared or changed and roughly when, alongside a current register of what stands on it now.

Used in: Project finance & ESIA · Renewables · Agriculture, forestry & nature

Request a proposal Imagery and data sources

What it is

The land history nobody wrote down

Land rarely comes with a history. A lender financing a solar plant, a company acquiring onshore assets or a plantation, or a developer choosing between candidate sites often inherits whatever happened on the land before: a village that grew into the site, clearing that began after a permit was issued, a road that brought settlement to the concession edge.

An imagery history reconstructs what can be seen. We gather the archived satellite imagery and open datasets that cover your area, date each observation to the images either side of it, and set out what was built, cleared or changed, and roughly when. A current register of the structures on the land today, and a land-use and land-cover baseline, complete the picture at the decision date.

Where the history may be relied on later, it can be packaged as an evidence pack with file fingerprints and an independent timestamp, fixing what was known at completion.

Why we write “roughly when”

An image shows the land on the day it was captured. A change between two images happened somewhere in between, so every date in the history is a window, not a day. The report shows the window and the sources either side of it.

How it works

From archive search to a dated history

  1. Area and question

    You send the parcel, route or site and what the history must answer: when settlement began, when clearing happened, what stood there at a given date.

  2. Archive search

    We check which dated very-high-resolution scenes exist in commercial archives, and which open datasets cover the area, before scoping the work.

  3. Reconstruct

    Reviewers work through the dated imagery in order, recording what appears, disappears or changes, alongside year-by-year trends in built-up land and land cover from open datasets.

  4. Now, and the record

    We add the current state: a register of structures on the land and within any corridor or hazard zone. The history and register can be packaged as an evidence pack.

Open datasets used are credited as their licences require, including Google Open Buildings (CC BY 4.0), ESA WorldCover (CC BY 4.0) and Copernicus Sentinel data. See imagery and data sources.

What you receive

A history your due-diligence team can cite

  • A dated timeline of what was built, cleared or changed, each entry with its date window and sources
  • Before-and-after views for the key changes, from the dated imagery named in the report
  • A land-use and land-cover baseline at the decision date: built-up land, cropland, bare ground, water and tree cover
  • Settlement growth trends around the site or route, as an area-level picture
  • A current structure register for the land, any right of way or boundary, and any hazard zone
  • Archive scenes used in the analysis, delivered as imagery where the supplier’s terms allow
  • An evidence pack, where scoped, and a PDF report in English or Portuguese with GIS layers

The services behind it

Every proposal names the services it includes. These are the ones this solution draws on.

Encroachment and structure mapping

  • Right-of-way encroachment surveyA register of the structures within the distances you choose from your pipeline, power line, road or railway. Each structure comes with its distance to the line and its coordinates, and each stretch of the route gets an encroachment-density rating.
  • Concession, site and boundary encroachment surveyStructures inside your concession, site or land-use boundary, in a ring around it, or both, mapped and listed so you can see where land is being occupied.
  • Structures in hazard and impact zonesStructures inside the zones you define, such as tailings dam-break inundation areas, blast and exclusion zones, flood lines or safety setbacks, each listed with its location and distance to the source.

Change and repeat surveys

  • Settlement growth trendsHow built-up land has changed year by year around your assets, showing where settlement pressure is growing.

Land and social baselines

  • Evidence packs for legal and community processesDated imagery, structure registers and maps packaged with file fingerprints and an independent timestamp, so you can show what was on the ground and when.
  • Imagery history and land due diligenceThe documented history of a parcel, route or site from archived satellite imagery and open datasets: what was built, cleared or changed, and roughly when.
  • Land-use and land-cover baselineA baseline map of built-up land, cropland, bare ground, water and tree cover around your project, combined with our structure register.

Drone and imagery

  • Very-high-resolution satellite imagery sourcingDated, very-high-resolution satellite scenes of your area sourced from commercial archives, used in your analysis and delivered as imagery.

Limits

What an imagery history is not

What it shows

  • What dated imagery shows on the land over time, and roughly when it changed
  • Where settlement and clearing have grown around the site
  • What stands on the land at the decision date

What it does not show

  • Title, ownership, tenure, valuation or liability
  • A compliance determination under any regulation
  • Anything in periods or places the archive does not cover
  • Who built, cleared or used the land

Frequently asked questions

How far back can you go?

It depends on the place. Archive coverage, dates and cloud vary a great deal, so we check what exists for your area before we scope the work and tell you which periods the history can and cannot cover. The report dates each observation to the images either side of it, which is why we write “roughly when”.

Is this a title or tenure check?

No. It shows what the imagery shows: structures, clearing, cultivation, water and change over time. Title, ownership, tenure, valuation and the legal status of any land use are for your lawyers, the cadastre and the relevant authorities.

Can it support an EU Deforestation Regulation assessment?

It can support one, by documenting tree cover, clearing and land use on each plot before and after the regulation’s cut-off date of 31 December 2020, where suitable imagery exists. It is not a compliance determination; that stays with the operator placing the product on the market.

Our insurer or lender wants to know what was there before. Can you help?

Yes, as a documented history for their assessment: what the imagery shows, on which dates, from which sources. It is not a valuation, a risk rating or a loss assessment.

Do you use web-map basemaps for the history?

No. Basemaps carry no capture date, so they cannot show when something happened. The history is built only from imagery and datasets with known dates, each named and credited in the report.

Tell us which land you are about to take on.

Send the parcel, route or site and the decision date. We check what archive imagery exists before we scope the work, and reply with a written proposal.
